  • 7:00pmThe Ballad of Suzanne Cesaire | New Americas Cinema IU CINEMA
    + Add to calendarGoogle Calendar
    via IU Cinema Report a problem or remove

    Based on the life of writer and feminist activist Suzanne Césaire, Madeleine Hunt-Ehrlich's debut feature explores the relationships with Césaire's husband, French politician Aimé Césaire, and fellow surrealist André Breton. Shimmering with the radiance of its Caribbean landscape and a phenomenal performance from Zita Hanrot, the film breaks from traditional biographical structure, blending more conventional narrative with captivating experimental elements. [75 min; biography, drama; English and French with English subtitles]

  • All dayThe Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment LILLY LIBRARY
    + Add to calendarGoogle Calendar
    via IU Arts & Humanities Institute Report a problem or remove

    The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless…

  • 9:00amHome Away from Home: Student Life on Campus HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
    + Add to calendarGoogle Calendar
    via IU Bloomington Libraries Report a problem or remove

    Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades - 1970s to the 2000s - items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.

  • 1:00pmOpen Studio SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
    + Add to calendarGoogle Calendar
    via Architecture + Design Report a problem or remove

    Our Open Studio program invites participants to create in the museum's art studio, where art becomes a tool for reflection, expression, and connection. Guided by a trained art therapist, the open studio welcomes visitors to engage with materials at their own pace while drawing inspiration from the surrounding exhibitions. No art experience is needed; just bring your curiosity and a desire to create, and we'll handle the rest! Participants are welcome to utilize supplies located in the studio, as well as bring their own supplies/projects to work on. This group meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. It is open to everyone: students, staff, and the public included! The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

  • 8:00pmOpen Mic Night at The Comedy Attic The Comedy Attic, 123 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
    + Add to calendarGoogle Calendar
    via Pillar Arts Community Calendar Report a problem or remove

    Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night! Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is. Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!
